subject: Hosted API quickstart — endpoints, rate limits, and deployment preference
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2024 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API quickstart — endpoints, rate limits, and deployment preference

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for the demo time earlier — really appreciate you walking us through Brightbridge's ingestion pipeline and the latency expectations for the live traffic. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our call:
- Primary use: assistant/agent responses and short-form extraction for customer support workflows.
- Typical baseline: ~30 qps steady, with peaks up to ~120 qps for 5–10 minute bursts.
- Latency target: P95 ~250–350ms for single-turn text generation.
- Data sensitivity: some records include PII; you flagged potential policy/regulatory constraints in EU.

Recommendation:
- Start with Hosted API for the pilot to get you running fast (sandbox endpoints, no infra setup).
- Keep Dedicated/Private in scope for longer-term (if you need VPC or on-prem for data residency) — we can map migration path and timelines.

What I need from you to scope the pilot properly:
1) Confirm if you want the sandbox in us-east or eu-west (affects data residency and regional routing).
2) Share a 24–48 hour sample traffic file (timestamps + payload sizes + qps) or a short doc describing peak cadence.
3) Confirm whether retention needs to be >30 days for logs/outputs (we can toggle retention and SOC2 controls).

Quickstart details (what you'll get):
- Sandbox endpoint (shared key) mapped to a test model (Open Llama 13B variant or similar)
- Default rate policy for trials: 60 req/min with automatic burst to 120 req/min (subject to fair-use; we can raise this for the pilot)
- Example endpoint: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate/brightbridge-test (we'll send credentials)
- Attach: hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf (steps for onboarding + sample curl)

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm region + share sample traffic (item 1–2 above) by EOD Tue.
- Me: provision sandbox creds and share endpoint details + SE availability for a tech deep-dive (I suggest Marissa on Thursday morning).

If Hosted proves functionally sufficient for the pilot, we can discuss a Dedicated pool sizing and pricing that meets your steady QPS and peak burst needs, or schedule Private/VPC evaluation for EU-only residency.

Short and sweet — let me know region preference and if you'd like me to provision sandbox now.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0182

Attachment: hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf (1 page checklist)
From: Tom Reynolds <tom@brightbridge.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2024 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart — endpoints, rate limits, and deployment preference

Thanks Stephanie — good recap and precisely the questions we had. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Region: prefer us-east to keep latency low for our US users but we have a subset of EU customers; can you confirm how data residency and logs are handled if we start in us-east?
- Traffic profile: baseline ~30 qps, but we see spikes to 120 qps for 5–12 minutes during nightly batch windows and product announcements.
- Retention: would like logs/outputs kept for 90 days for debugging in early stages. Any cost impact?
- Cost sensitivity: we want to avoid committing to Dedicated unless the cost-per-inference improves substantially for steady-state; starting Hosted is preferred for speed.

Can you send sandbox creds and a sample curl for the endpoint? Also appreciate a short note on how easy it is to migrate to Dedicated/VPC later without code changes.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director, Platform Engineering
Brightbridge
tom@brightbridge.com
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jan 2024 18:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart — endpoints, rate limits, and deployment preference

On Thu, Jan 18, 2024 at 6:02 PM Tom Reynolds <tom@brightbridge.com> wrote:
> Thanks Stephanie — good recap and precisely the questions we had. A few clarifications from our side: 
> 
> - Region: prefer us-east to keep latency low for our US users but we have a subset of EU customers; can you confirm how data residency and logs are handled if we start in us-east?
> - Traffic profile: baseline ~30 qps, but we see spikes to 120 qps for 5–12 minutes during nightly batch windows and product announcements.
> - Retention: would like logs/outputs kept for 90 days for debugging in early stages. Any cost impact?
> - Cost sensitivity: we want to avoid committing to Dedicated unless the cost-per-inference improves substantially for steady-state; starting Hosted is preferred for speed.

Thanks for the clarifications — answers inline below: 

- Data residency: if you start in us-east, request data (requests + logs) are routed and stored in the selected region. For EU customers we can provision a separate tenant/endpoint in eu-west; or, if you need a VPC with EU-only egress, we recommend Private (longer lead time).
- Retention: 90-day retention is fine for pilot; there is a small incremental storage charge (~$X/month for your expected volume). We'll surface exact numbers once we have sample traffic.
- Bursts: Hosted trial policy allows controlled bursts to 120 req/min. For sustained peaks above that we recommend a Dedicated pool or raising rate with an interim uplift (short term).
- Migration: code-level changes are minimal — same API paths and SDKs. You can pin model versions and switch routing policy in the Console. We'll document the exact steps in the quickstart doc.

I attached the hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf which includes: sandbox provisioning steps, sample curl (with a masked API key), how to request rate increases, and migration notes.

Propose a 30-minute technical deep-dive with Marissa to validate your payload sizes, confirm tokenization behavior, and run a small load test. Are you available Thursday 11:00am PT or Friday 9:00am PT?

I'll provision a sandbox (us-east) as soon as you confirm — I'll include a short-lived API key and sample endpoint in the provisioning email.

Best,
Stephanie

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom@brightbridge.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jan 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API quickstart — endpoints, rate limits, and deployment preference

Hi Tom / Stephanie —

Following up with the technical specifics I promised:

- Sandbox endpoint (example): https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate/brightbridge-test
- Sample curl (masked key):
  curl -X POST "https://sandbox.redwood.ai/v1/generate/brightbridge-test" -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-XXXXX' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"prompt":"Summarize the following support ticket:","max_tokens":256}'

- Rate limits for trial: 60 req/min by default, automated short bursts to 120 req/min. For production we offer rate tiers (200/min, 500/min, above) tied to capacity commitments.
- Throughput notes: if your average payload is small (under 300 tokens), the baseline P95 at 30 qps on Hosted in us-east should be within your 250–350ms target using an optimized model. Larger context windows increase latency.
- Migration: endpoints and SDKs are identical between Hosted and Dedicated; migration is largely a routing/tuning exercise — we provide a migration playbook and can run a smoke test in staging.

I'd be happy to run a 10–15 minute baseline load test against your sample payloads once you share them. For the deep-dive I can cover batching behavior and KV/pre-prefix caching recommendations to reduce token cost.

Availability: Thursday 11:00am PT works for me (I'll add a calendar invite).

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: hosted_quickstart_checklist.pdf (referenced above)
